questions.q: This lab's Resource has relative path /checkout/{sys_id} under Version v1, base path /api/x_acme_eqchk. What is the full URL a caller hits?
options: /api/x_acme_eqchk/checkout/v1/{sys_id}
/v1/api/x_acme_eqchk/checkout/{sys_id}
/api/x_acme_eqchk/v1/checkout/{sys_id}
/api/checkout/x_acme_eqchk/v1/{sys_id}
questions.explain: The Version's segment (v1) sits between the API's base path and the Resource's own relative path: /api/x_acme_eqchk/v1/checkout/{sys_id}.

questions.q: In the script, if (!gr.get(requestId)) { response.setStatus(404); ... return; } — what does gr.get() return when no x_acme_eqchk_request record matches that sys_id?
options: An exception that stops the script before setStatus can run
undefined, which the script ignores and proceeds to build a result anyway
true, and the script then builds a result object from empty fields
false, which is exactly the signal the script uses to answer with a 404
questions.explain: gr.get() returns false on no match, which is checked with ! before setting status 404 and returning early.

questions.q: var includeHistory = request.queryParams.include_history === 'true'; — why the explicit === 'true' comparison?
options: Because queryParams always returns a number that needs comparing
Because === 'true' is required syntax for every REST API script regardless of the value's type
Because queryParams values are always strings or undefined, never real booleans, so the comparison is what converts it into one
Because omitting it would cause a runtime error rather than a wrong default
questions.explain: request.queryParams values come through as strings (or undefined); the === 'true' check is what turns that into an actual boolean.

questions.q: gr.equipment.equipment_name.toString() appears in the result object. What is this doing?
options: Querying a second, unrelated table with a fresh GlideRecord call
Reading a field that lives directly on x_acme_eqchk_request, not a referenced table
Dot-walking the equipment reference field to read the related equipment record's own name
Converting the entire request record into a single string
questions.explain: equipment is a reference field on x_acme_eqchk_request; dot-walking through it reaches the referenced x_acme_eqchk_equipment record's equipment_name.

questions.q: Per the lab, what could a v2 of this API add without touching v1's script at all?
options: A change to what status code v1 returns for a missing record
A computed is_overdue flag, or a list-all-checkouts Resource with no sys_id, each as its own new Resource under a new Version
Removing the required-roles setting from the API definition
Nothing — any new field requires rewriting v1's existing script directly
questions.explain: v2 additions live in their own Resource scripts under their own Version — v1's script, and therefore its behavior, never changes.
